title: Language Resolution
description: The one protocol every runtime (TypeScript, Go, Rust, Python oracle) reads to choose the language of texts; no language is ever assumed. A command refuses without a choice, a notice is written in every offered language.

flag.description: The command-line flag, as `--lang <value>` or `--lang=<value>`; the last one before `argumentsEnd` counts.

argumentsEnd.description: Arguments after this one belong to a child command and are never read.

explicitVariable.description: The variable that chooses the language explicitly; it must name an offered language.

preferenceListVariable.description: The GNU preference list; its first offered entry counts.

environmentOrder.description: The POSIX locale variables; only the first non-empty one is read (LC_ALL=C overrides LANG).

subtagSeparators.description: Characters that end the language subtag of a locale or tag (`de_CH.UTF-8@euro`, `en-US`).

withoutChoice.description: What happens when the arguments and the environment name no offered language: a command reads the operating system language list and refuses with every way to choose a language when that names none either; a notice (progress, warning, refusal text of a library) is written in every offered language and never reads the operating system, so one environment gives the same notice on every machine. A command exports its choice as `explicitVariable` to its children, so their notices speak its language.

osLocale.description: The operating system language list, read last and by commands only.

pattern.description: Its first capture group is one language tag of the command output.

refusal.description: The refusal of a command, one line per offered language; `{choice}` lists the offered languages.
